candidates.source_name: EBA — Consultation papers (all open/closed consultations, with response deadlines)
candidates.why_relevant: Primary EU-level origin of binding technical standards and guidelines that Banka Slovenije and SI banks/PSPs must apply. Each paper carries an explicit response deadline and public-hearing date, giving 3-12 months of lead time before Slovenian applicability.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML scrape of the filtered listing (status=open) plus PDF capture; extract title, publication date, deadline, mandate reference (CRR3/PSD3/PSR/DORA/DGSD3).
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from law-firm regulatory trackers
queries_used: EBA consultation papers PSD3 PSR response deadline 2026 interactive single rulebook

candidates.source_name: EBA — Interactive Single Rulebook / Regulation and policy hub
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical index mapping Level 1 EU acts to the RTS/ITS/Guidelines under them, with application dates. Best single pointer for enumerating what will bind Slovenian institutions and when.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl topic index pages; snowball into individual instrument pages for dates of application.
candidates.discovered_via_method: structural inference from EBA site architecture
queries_used: EBA consultation papers PSD3 PSR response deadline 2026 interactive single rulebook

candidates.source_name: EBA — Guidelines compliance tables (national competent authority 'comply or explain', incl. Banka Slovenije)
candidates.why_relevant: The compliance table attached to each EBA guideline states explicitly whether Banka Slovenije complies, intends to comply (with date), or does not — the single most direct evidence of Slovenian applicability of an EU-level soft-law instrument.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: For each guideline page, fetch the 'Compliance table' PDF and parse the row for SI / Banka Slovenije.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language seed query snowballed to EBA compliance-table mechanism
queries_used: EBA smernice Banka Slovenije izjava o skladnosti compliance table

candidates.source_name: EBA — Slovenian-language translations of Guidelines (Translations sub-library)
candidates.why_relevant: EBA publishes each guideline in Slovenian ('Smernice'). These SL PDFs are the terminology bridge between EU-level text and Slovenian supervisory/industry language, and are what SI institutions actually cite.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest document_library PDF URLs containing '_SL' under /Translations/; use for glossary building.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search returning SL EBA PDFs directly
queries_used: EBA smernice Banka Slovenije izjava o skladnosti compliance table

candidates.source_name: EBA — Opinions and Reports (incl. transition-period opinions)
candidates.why_relevant: EBA Opinions frequently set or clarify supervisory expectations and end-dates (e.g. Opinion EBA/OP/2026/01 on the end of the NAL transition period) that NCAs including Banka Slovenije then apply.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll publications listing filtered by type=Opinion/Report; store PDF + date.
queries_used: EBA consultation papers PSD3 PSR response deadline 2026 interactive single rulebook

candidates.source_name: EBA — Credit institutions / payment institutions registers (EUCLID-based public registers)
candidates.why_relevant: Pan-EU register listing authorised credit institutions and PSD2 payment/e-money institutions per Member State, including SI entities and passporting into Slovenia. Structural map of who is in scope of the rules.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic bulk download of register extracts filtered on home/host country = SI.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles category inference (who must publish authorisation data)

candidates.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — List of supervised entities (SI / LSI, monthly PDF + data)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative determination of which Slovenian banks are ECB-supervised significant institutions (NLB Group; Gorenjska Banka via AikGroup; OTP's SI operations via OTP Luxembourg) versus LSIs left to Banka Slovenije. Directly defines the SI-designated-significant perimeter for this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly fetch of the list PDF/CSV; diff SI-country rows to detect designation changes.
queries_used: ECB list of supervised entities Slovenia significant institutions NLB SSM

candidates.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — SSM supervisory priorities and risk assessment
candidates.why_relevant: Annual multi-year priorities set the examination and thematic-review agenda that flows down to SI-designated significant institutions and, via Banka Slovenije, to LSIs. Strong leading indicator of where supervisory pressure (and vendor demand) will land.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch (typically December) plus SREP aggregate results.
queries_used: ECB SSM significant institutions Slovenia supervisory priorities

candidates.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — Public consultations (guides, ECB Regulations, options and discretions)
candidates.why_relevant: ECB consultations on supervisory guides and ECB Regulations carry hard response deadlines and later become directly applicable to SI-designated significant institutions without national transposition.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape consultation listing; capture deadline and feedback statement when published.
candidates.discovered_via_method: structural inference from ECB legal-framework section
queries_used: ECB SSM significant institutions Slovenia supervisory priorities

candidates.source_name: ECB — Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) implementation hub
candidates.why_relevant: Central reference for IPR application dates (reachability, sending, VoP, sanctions screening) that bind every euro-area PSP including all Slovenian banks. Directly drives SI vendor/procurement timelines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic page fetch + diff; follow linked ECB/Eurosystem statements.
queries_used: instant payments regulation application date verification of payee

candidates.source_name: ECB AMI-Pay / AMI-SeCo market group meeting documents
candidates.why_relevant: Meeting packs contain unusually candid deployment status updates (e.g. EPC's May 2026 VoP deployment presentation) months ahead of formal publication — an early-warning channel on payments-scheme readiness relevant to SI PSPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest per-meeting document lists (PDF) on a quarterly cadence.
queries_used: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook SEPA instant credit transfer 2026 documents

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council — Document library (rulebooks, incl. VoP Scheme Rulebook v1.1)
candidates.why_relevant: EPC scheme rulebooks (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD, VoP) are the operational rules Slovenian PSPs must implement to satisfy the IPR. Rulebook versions and effective dates are the concrete implementation deadlines behind the EU regulation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch rulebook pages for new version PDFs; extract version, entry-into-force date, and change requests.
queries_used: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook SEPA instant credit transfer 2026 documents

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council — Public consultations on scheme rulebook change requests
candidates.why_relevant: EPC runs 3-month public consultations on change requests (e.g. the SCT Inst consultation open to 11 June 2026). These are the earliest visible signal of scheme changes SI banks will have to fund.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the news/insights feed and the consultation pages; capture deadline dates.
queries_used: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook SEPA instant credit transfer 2026 documents

candidates.source_name: EPC — Register of Participants / scheme participant lists (Slovenian PSPs)
candidates.why_relevant: Shows which Slovenian PSPs have adhered to each EPC scheme, i.e. who is contractually bound and who is still to onboard — a concrete adoption-gap indicator for SI.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download participant register export, filter country=SI; URL path unverified — locate via site navigation.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles inference (schemes must publish adherence lists)

candidates.source_name: ESRB — National policy: countercyclical capital buffer, other measures, reciprocation (Slovenia rows)
candidates.why_relevant: Central EU register of Slovenian macroprudential measures (CCyB rate, systemic risk buffer for real-estate/household exposures, borrower-based measures) and of foreign measures Slovenia must reciprocate. Includes Banka Slovenije notification PDFs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the CCyB / other-measures / reciprocation tables and diff SI rows; archive linked notification PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed extension + snowball to SI notification document
queries_used: ESRB recommendation Slovenia countercyclical capital buffer reciprocation national measures register

candidates.source_name: ESRB — Recommendations and Warnings
candidates.why_relevant: ESRB recommendations carry 'act or explain' obligations with fixed compliance deadlines for addressees including Slovenian authorities; they often precede binding national measures by 12-24 months.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll listing; parse addressee and deadline sections of each recommendation PDF.
queries_used: ESRB recommendation Slovenia countercyclical capital buffer reciprocation national measures register

candidates.source_name: EUR-Lex — Uradni list Evropske unije, serija L (daily view, Slovenian)
candidates.why_relevant: The Slovenian-language Official Journal is the authentic legal text binding in Slovenia. Publication in OJ L fixes entry-into-force and application dates for CRR3, PSD3/PSR, DORA, IPR and their delegated acts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily poll of the L-series daily view in locale=sl; better, use the EUR-Lex SPARQL/Cellar API or expert-search RSS filtered on subject-matter codes for banking/payments.
queries_used: "Uradni list Evropske unije" slovenščina EUR-Lex uredba plačilne storitve

candidates.source_name: EUR-Lex — Slovenian legislation summaries and CELEX consolidated texts (payments/banking)
candidates.why_relevant: Consolidated SL texts and 'povzetki zakonodaje' give the Slovenian legal vocabulary (e.g. 'Uredba o enotnem območju plačil v eurih') used by Banka Slovenije and SI banks, and link each act to its implementing measures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve CELEX numbers to SL HTML/PDF; use for glossary and for tracking amendments to a watched act.
queries_used: "Uradni list Evropske unije" slovenščina EUR-Lex uredba plačilne storitve

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Regulativni okvir / Nadzorniška razkritja in seznami (SI landing point for EU rules)
candidates.why_relevant: Although a national body, these pages are the authoritative pointer showing HOW an EU instrument lands in Slovenia (which EBA guideline BS applies, supervisory disclosure tables under CRD, options and discretions). Essential to filter EU output for SI applicability.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the regulatory-framework and supervisory-disclosure pages; cross-join EBA guideline IDs to BS application statements.
queries_used: EBA smernice Banka Slovenije izjava o skladnosti compliance table

candidates.source_name: Bančni vestnik (ZBS) — Slovenian banking journal coverage of EU regulatory change
candidates.why_relevant: Slovenian Bank Association journal publishes practitioner articles interpreting EU instruments (e.g. 'Regulatorne spremembe s področja tveganj, povezanih z IKT' on DORA) — reveals how SI institutions read EU deadlines and where they see implementation pain.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor issue index; fetch open-access PDFs only, cite rather than redistribute.
queries_used: EBA smernice Banka Slovenije izjava o skladnosti compliance table

candidates.source_name: European Commission — Have your say (public consultations on EU financial services acts)
candidates.why_relevant: Level 1 consultations and delegated-act feedback periods for PSD3/PSR, FIDA, CRR3 amendments appear here with hard feedback deadlines, and are available in Slovenian. Earliest possible lead time in the EU pipeline.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the portal's topic filter (financial services) and RSS/export; capture feedback-period end dates.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles category inference (who initiates EU law)

candidates.source_name: Law-firm and consultancy EU regulatory trackers (Norton Rose 'Regulation Tomorrow', PwC Legal, KPMG, Morrison Foerster)
candidates.why_relevant: Fast, dated secondary summaries of EBA/ECB/Commission publications with implied timelines (PSD3/PSR expected in force late 2027, IPR milestones). Useful as a discovery tripwire and cross-check, never as primary evidence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/feed monitoring for alerting only; always resolve back to the primary EBA/ECB/OJ document.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball across multiple queries
queries_used: EBA consultation papers PSD3 PSR response deadline 2026 interactive single rulebook

negative_findings.description: Neither the EBA nor the ECB Banking Supervision consultation registers publish consultation papers or deadlines in Slovenian; only final Guidelines are translated into SL, and typically months after the consultation has closed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovenian-language searching surfaced EBA SL guideline PDFs but no SL-language consultation or deadline listing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any monitoring design that relies on Slovenian-language triggers will systematically miss the earliest (consultation-stage) lead time; EN monitoring of EU bodies is mandatory and SL is only usable downstream.

negative_findings.description: No EU-level source found that pre-filters EBA/ECB/ESRB output by Slovenian applicability. The only Slovenia-specific EU-level artefacts located were EBA guideline compliance tables (per-NCA rows) and ESRB national-policy tables (per-country rows).
negative_findings.result_summary: Country filtering must be constructed by the collector from these two per-country structures plus Banka Slovenije pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines the pipeline architecture: EU-wide harvest plus a derived SI-applicability join, rather than a country feed.

negative_findings.description: The EPC Register of Participants URL path was inferred from site structure, not confirmed by a fetch in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence (0.6); path may differ.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated-looking dead link from being treated as verified; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve it.

negative_findings.description: No stable Slovenian-language term was found in circulation for 'Verification of Payee' — SI and EU-SL material appears to use the English term or the EPC acronym VOP rather than a settled SL translation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language searching on VoP concepts is unreliable; use 'preverjanje prejemnika plačila' as a hypothesis only, and rely on EN/acronym matching.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects glossary quality and recall of SL-language payments monitoring.

coverage_gaps.description: Single Resolution Board (SRB) and the EU resolution stream (BRRD/SRMR, MREL decisions affecting NLB Group) were not scouted in this pass, although they are EU-level bodies binding on SI-designated significant institutions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add srb.europa.eu (public consultations, MREL policy, resolution planning cycle) as a follow-up cell or extension of this one.

coverage_gaps.description: ESMA, EIOPA and the AMLA (Anti-Money Laundering Authority, Frankfurt) were out of the stated cell but overlap heavily with payments/banking compliance deadlines in Slovenia (AMLR single rulebook from 2027).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign AMLA and the AML package to a dedicated cell; it is the largest missing EU-origin deadline stream for SI banks and PSPs.

coverage_gaps.description: No API/RSS endpoints were confirmed for EBA, ECB Banking Supervision, ESRB or EPC in this pass; only HTML landing pages. EUR-Lex is known to expose Cellar/SPARQL but this was not exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a technical probe pass for RSS/Atom feeds, sitemap.xml and open APIs on each domain before committing to HTML scraping.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian-language coverage in this cell rests on four anchors only: EUR-Lex SL, EBA SL guideline translations, Banka Slovenije pages, and Bančni vestnik. No SL-language EU-affairs news or parliamentary-scrutiny channel was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout SL-language secondary channels (Državni zbor EU-affairs committee documents, Ministrstvo za finance EU dossier pages, Finance.si / STA regulatory coverage) in an adjacent cell.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival strategy identified for consultation pages, which EBA/ECB remove or re-file once closed; historical deadline data may be recoverable only via web archives.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot consultation listings at collection time and register Wayback captures for key pages.

brief: For Slovenia, the binding regulatory calendar is written almost entirely at EU level and only annotated nationally: EUR-Lex's Slovenian-language Official Journal fixes the legally authentic dates, while EBA consultation papers, ECB/SSM consultations and supervisory priorities, EPC scheme rulebooks and ESRB national-policy tables supply 6-24 months of advance warning before anything appears in Slovenian practice. The Slovenia filter is not a country feed but a derived join: EBA per-NCA guideline compliance tables and the ECB list of supervised entities (NLB Group, Gorenjska Banka via AikGroup, OTP's SI operations) define who is bound, and Banka Slovenije's regulativni okvir and nadzorniška razkritja pages confirm how. Slovenian-language material exists downstream (EUR-Lex SL, EBA 'Smernice' translations, Bančni vestnik) but never at consultation stage, so English-language monitoring of EU bodies is structurally mandatory and SL is a terminology and confirmation layer. Highest-value targets are the EBA consultation register, EUR-Lex OJ L (SL daily view), the ECB IPR hub and the EPC rulebook library; the largest unscouted EU-origin deadline stream is the AML package under AMLA, plus SRB resolution policy.
